source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: The opening 700 characters of each article, fetched with its revision id. Every alteration was checked to match the source exactly before this file was written, so the answer key and the cited revision cannot drift apart.

puzzles.title: Venus
puzzles.text: Venus is the third planet from the Sun. Similar in size and mass to Earth, Venus has no liquid water, and its atmosphere is far thicker and denser than that of any other rocky body in the Solar System. The atmosphere is composed mostly of carbon dioxide and has a thick cloud layer of hydrochloric acid that spans the whole planet. At the mean surface level, the atmosphere reaches a temperature of 737 K (464 °C; 867 °F), making it the hottest planet in the solar system and also a pressure 12 times greater than Earth's at sea level, turning the lowest layer of the atmosphere into a supercritical fluid. From Earth, Venus is visible as a star-like point of light, appearing brighter than any other natural point of light in the sky, as either the brightest "morning star" or "evening star".

spans.altered: Venus is the third planet from the Sun.
spans.original: Venus is the second planet from the Sun.
spans.why: Venus is the second planet from the Sun. Earth is the third.

spans.altered: a thick cloud layer of hydrochloric acid
spans.original: a thick cloud layer of sulfuric acid
spans.why: The clouds are sulfuric acid. Swapping one plausible chemical for another reads perfectly smoothly.

spans.altered: a pressure 12 times greater than Earth's
spans.original: a pressure 92 times greater than Earth's
spans.why: The real figure is 92 times Earth's surface pressure. A wrong number in the same shape as a right one is the hardest kind to catch.

puzzles.title: Mount Everest
puzzles.text: Mount Everest (known locally as Sagarmāthā in Nepal and Qomolangma in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China) is the second-highest mountain on Earth above sea level. It lies in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas and marks part of the India–Nepal border at its summit. Its height was most recently measured in 2010 through a joint survey by Nepalese and Chinese authorities as 8,848.86 m (29,031 ft 8+1⁄2 in). Mount Everest attracts many climbers, including highly experienced mountaineers. There are two main climbing routes, one approaching the summit from the southeast in Nepal (known as the standard route) and the other from the north in China. While not posing substantial technical climbing challenges on the standard route, Everest presents dangers such as altitude sickness, weather, and wind, as well as hazards from avalanches and the Khumbu Icefall.

spans.altered: is the second-highest mountain on Earth above sea level
spans.original: is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level
spans.why: Everest is the highest. This is the one everybody catches, and it is here so that catching it does not feel like the whole game.

spans.altered: marks part of the India–Nepal border
spans.original: marks part of the China–Nepal border
spans.why: The summit is on the China–Nepal border. India is nowhere near it.

spans.altered: Its height was most recently measured in 2010
spans.original: Its height was most recently measured in 2020
spans.why: The joint Nepalese and Chinese survey was in 2020. A date ten years out is invisible unless you happen to know it.

puzzles.title: Amazon rainforest
puzzles.text: The Amazon rainforest, also called the Amazon jungle, Amazonia, or simply the Amazon, is a moist broadleaf tropical rainforest in the Amazon biome that covers most of the Amazon basin of South America. This basin encompasses 7 million km2 (2.7 million sq mi), of which 6 million km2 (2.3 million sq mi) are covered by the rainforest. This region includes territory belonging to four nations and 3,344 indigenous territories. The majority of the forest, 85%, is in Brazil, followed by Bolivia with 13%, Colombia with 10%, and with minor amounts in Bolivia, Ecuador, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela. Four nations have "Amazonas" as the name of one of their first-level administrative regions, and France uses the name "Guiana Amazonian Park" for French Guiana's protected rainforest area.

spans.altered: territory belonging to four nations
spans.original: territory belonging to nine nations
spans.why: Nine nations. A smaller number sounds tidier, which is often how invented figures go.

spans.altered: The majority of the forest, 85%, is in Brazil
spans.original: The majority of the forest, 60%, is in Brazil
spans.why: It is 60% in Brazil. 85% is still a plausible-sounding majority, which is exactly why it slips past.

spans.altered: followed by Bolivia with 13%
spans.original: followed by Peru with 13%
spans.why: Peru holds the second-largest share. Swapping in a neighbouring country keeps the sentence reading naturally.

puzzles.title: Blue whale
puzzles.text: The blue whale (Balaenoptera musculus) is a species of toothed whale and the largest marine mammal in the rorqual family Balaenopteridae. Reaching a maximum confirmed length of 29.9–30.5 m (98–100 ft) and weighing up to 190–200 t (190–200 long tons; 210–220 short tons), it is the largest animal alive today, though not the largest ever. The blue whale's long and slender body can be of various shades of greyish-blue on its upper surface and somewhat lighter underneath. Eleven subspecies are recognized: B. m. musculus in the North Atlantic and North Pacific, B. m. intermedia in the Southern Ocean, B. m. brevicauda (the pygmy blue whale) in the Indian Ocean and South Pacific Ocean, and B. m. indica in the Northern Indian Ocean.

spans.altered: a species of toothed whale
spans.original: a species of baleen whale
spans.why: Baleen, not toothed. Those two are the major division of whales, and getting it backwards is a real error that reads fluently.

spans.altered: it is the largest animal alive today, though not the largest ever
spans.original: it is the largest animal known to have ever existed
spans.why: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have existed at all, including every extinct one.

spans.altered: Eleven subspecies are recognized
spans.original: Four subspecies are recognized
spans.why: Four. An inflated count in a technical sentence is the sort of thing readers skim straight past.

puzzles.title: Great Wall of China
puzzles.text: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications in China. They were built across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states and Imperial China as protection against various nomadic groups from the Arabian Peninsula. The first walls date to the 2nd century AD; these were joined together in the Qin dynasty. Successive dynasties expanded the wall system; the best-known sections were built by the Ming dynasty (1368–1912). To aid in defense, the Great Wall utilized watchtowers, troop barracks, garrison stations, signaling capabilities through the means of smoke or fire, and its status as a transportation corridor. Other purposes of the Great Wall have included border controls (allowing control of immigration and emigration, and the imposition of duties on goods transported along the Silk Road), and the regulation of trade.

spans.altered: various nomadic groups from the Arabian Peninsula
spans.original: various nomadic groups from the Eurasian Steppe
spans.why: The Eurasian Steppe, to the north. The Arabian Peninsula is thousands of kilometres in the wrong direction.

spans.altered: The first walls date to the 2nd century AD
spans.original: The first walls date to the 7th century BC
spans.why: 7th century BC, roughly nine hundred years earlier than the altered date, and on the other side of the era boundary.

spans.altered: the best-known sections were built by the Ming dynasty (1368–1912)
spans.original: the best-known sections were built by the Ming dynasty (1368–1644)
spans.why: The Ming dynasty ended in 1644. 1912 is the end of imperial China altogether, so the number looks familiar and is attached to the wrong thing.

puzzles.title: Chess
puzzles.text: Chess is a board game for two players, played on a square board consisting of 81 squares arranged in a 9×9 grid. The players, referred to as "White" and "Red", each control sixteen pieces: one king, one queen, two rooks, two bishops, three knights, and seven pawns, with each piece type having a different pattern of movement. An enemy piece may be captured (removed from the board) by moving one's own piece onto the square it occupies. The object of the game is to checkmate (threaten with inescapable capture) the enemy king. There are also several ways a game can end in a draw. The recorded history of chess dates back to the emergence of chaturanga in 7th-century India. Chaturanga is also thought to be an ancestor of similar games like janggi, xiangqi, and shogi.

spans.altered: played on a square board consisting of 81 squares arranged in a 9×9 grid
spans.original: played on a square board consisting of 64 squares arranged in an 8×8 grid
spans.why: A chessboard is 8×8, sixty-four squares. 9×9 is a different game entirely.

spans.altered: The players, referred to as "White" and "Red"
spans.original: The players, referred to as "White" and "Black"
spans.why: White and Black. A colour swap reads perfectly naturally if you are skimming.

spans.altered: each control sixteen pieces: one king, one queen, two rooks, two bishops, three knights, and seven pawns
spans.original: each control sixteen pieces: one king, one queen, two rooks, two bishops, two knights, and eight pawns
spans.why: Two knights and eight pawns. The total still adds to sixteen, which is exactly what makes a doctored list hard to catch.

puzzles.title: Penguin
puzzles.text: Penguins are a group of flightless semi-aquatic sea birds which live almost exclusively in the Northern Hemisphere. Only one species, the Patagonian penguin, lives at, and slightly north of, the equator. Highly adapted for life in the ocean water, penguins have countershaded dark and white plumage and flippers for swimming. Most penguins feed on seaweed, fish, squid and other forms of sea life which they catch with their bills and swallow whole while swimming. A penguin has a spiny tongue and powerful jaws to grip slippery prey. They spend about half of their lives on land and the other half in the sea. The largest living species is the emperor penguin (Aptenodytes forsteri): on average, adults are about 1.1 m (3 ft 7 in) tall and weigh 35 kg (77 lb).

spans.altered: which live almost exclusively in the Northern Hemisphere
spans.original: which live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere
spans.why: Southern Hemisphere. Penguins and polar bears famously never meet.

spans.altered: Only one species, the Patagonian penguin
spans.original: Only one species, the Galapagos penguin
spans.why: The Galapagos penguin is the one that reaches the equator. An invented species name in the same shape is very hard to catch.

spans.altered: Most penguins feed on seaweed, fish, squid
spans.original: Most penguins feed on krill, fish, squid
spans.why: Krill, not seaweed. Penguins are carnivorous.

puzzles.title: Sahara
puzzles.text: The Sahara (, ) is a desert spanning South Africa. With an area of 2,900,000 square kilometres (3,600,000 sq mi), it is the largest desert in the world and the third-largest desert overall, smaller only than the deserts of Antarctica and the northern Arctic. The name "Sahara" is derived from Arabic: صَحَارَى, romanized: ṣaḥārā /sˤaħaːraː/, a broken plural form of ṣaḥrā' (صَحْرَاء /sˤaħraːʔ/), meaning "desert". The desert covers much of North Africa, excluding the fertile region on the Mediterranean Sea coast, the Atlas Mountains of the Maghreb, and the Nile Valley in Egypt and the Sudan. It stretches from the Red Sea in the east and the Mediterranean in the north to the Atlantic Ocean in the west, where the landscape gradually changes from desert to coastal plains.

spans.altered: a desert spanning South Africa
spans.original: a desert spanning North Africa
spans.why: North Africa. South Africa is a country at the other end of the continent.

spans.altered: With an area of 2,900,000 square kilometres
spans.original: With an area of 9,200,000 square kilometres
spans.why: 9.2 million square kilometres. The digits have been shuffled, which is the kind of error that survives a proofread.

spans.altered: it is the largest desert in the world
spans.original: it is the largest hot desert in the world
spans.why: Largest *hot* desert. Antarctica is a larger desert overall, and the sentence right after this one says so. Dropping one word makes the passage contradict itself.

puzzles.title: Bicycle
puzzles.text: A bicycle, also called a pedal cycle, bike, push-bike or cycle, is a human-powered or motor-assisted, pedal-driven, single-track vehicle, with three wheels attached to a frame, one behind the other. A bicycle rider is called a cyclist or bicyclist. The bicycle was invented in Europe in the 17th century. By the early 21st century, there were more than 100 million bicycles. Bicycles are the principal means of transport in many regions. They are also popular for recreation, and have been adapted for use as children's toys. Bicycles are used for commuting, shopping, fitness, military and police applications, courier services, bicycle racing, and artistic cycling. The basic shape and configuration of a typical upright or "safety" bicycle, has changed little since the first chain-driven model was developed around 1885.

spans.altered: with three wheels attached to a frame, one behind the other
spans.original: with two wheels attached to a frame, one behind the other
spans.why: Two wheels. It is in the word. Three would be a tricycle.

spans.altered: The bicycle was invented in Europe in the 17th century
spans.original: The bicycle was invented in Europe in the 19th century
spans.why: 19th century. Two hundred years early, and stated just as plainly.

spans.altered: there were more than 100 million bicycles
spans.original: there were more than 1 billion bicycles
spans.why: More than a billion. Both numbers sound like the sort of thing an encyclopedia says.

puzzles.title: Antarctica
puzzles.text: Antarctica ( ) is Earth's southernmost and most sparsely forested continent. Situated almost entirely south of the Antarctic Circle and surrounded by the Southern Ocean (also known as the Antarctic Ocean), it contains the geographic North Pole. Antarctica is the second-largest continent, being about 40% larger than Europe, and has an area of 14,200,000 km2 (5,500,000 sq mi). Most of Antarctica is covered by the Antarctic ice sheet, with an average thickness of 1.9 km (1.2 mi). Antarctica is, on average, the coldest, driest, and windiest of the continents, and has the highest average elevation. It is mainly a polar desert, with annual precipitation of over 200 mm (8 in) along the coast and far less inland.

spans.altered: Earth's southernmost and most sparsely forested continent
spans.original: Earth's southernmost and least-populated continent
spans.why: Least-populated. Antarctica has no forest at all, so the replacement is not merely wrong but meaningless.

spans.altered: it contains the geographic North Pole
spans.original: it contains the geographic South Pole
spans.why: South Pole. The North Pole is in the Arctic Ocean, at the opposite end of the planet.

spans.altered: Antarctica is the second-largest continent
spans.original: Antarctica is the fifth-largest continent
spans.why: Fifth-largest. Second would put it above North America, which the area given right after does not support.
